svg.text: gestate — the whole thing on one sheet

A language that describes music, pictures and sound, and the host that performs what it describes. Generated by python -m gestate.atlas — every box is a file that exists and every arrow an import that is there.

Lanes and spine are declared in gestate/atlas.py; modules, libraries and crates are read from the tree. test_atlas.py fails when this sheet is not what the source renders — then run the command above.
A .ges file and the libraries in scope for it — each
backend looks for one declaration. The two below read
this tree and write it back out: doc/ref/, and this
Text to declarations: tokens, layout, patterns, the
prelude that every file is assembled with.
Inference, classes and their instances, the Datafun and
audio subgrammars — every refusal is written here.
Supercombinators on a graph machine, in Python for the
reference and in Rust (crust) for the window.
score and bpm, performed to timed events.
substrate : Sig Sub, forced at frame rate.
writes a window, and a plugin tab
sound : Sig Float leaves the interpreter: the first-order fragment is extracted
to a graph, the graph to C, the C to a .so by clang.
The window, the painter, the plugin and the audio callback. The G-machine is
here twice on purpose: the Python one is the reference the other answers to.
command.ges is the command list; the model holds the text and what is playing,
The engine fills a buffer, the C host owns the card, and an edit is installed
under the sound without stopping it.
